protocol.name: recon_theme_v1
protocol.copyright: Public domain, like the rest of ReconOS. See LICENSE.txt.

description.summary: tells a client what the desktop looks like

protocol.description:
ReconOS draws its own windows, menus and text, and the applications that ship with it read the palette directly. An application that arrives later is a Wayland client in its own process and cannot: it has no way to know what colour a button is on this desktop, or that somebody has just changed it.
Without this, a client has three options and all of them are bad. It can guess, and be the one window that does not match. It can ship its own theme, and be the one window that does not change when the desktop does. Or it can read the registry behind the compositor's back, which works until the format changes and is not a boundary at all.
So the compositor says. A client binds this, is told the whole palette at once, and is told again whenever it changes.
---
On the shape of it: the palette is sent as a run of colours in a fixed order rather than as a colour per event with a name attached. That order is ReconOS's own role enum and the protocol is versioned against it, which means adding a role is a new version rather than a silent change in the length of an array. Names would survive that better and would cost a string per role per change, forty-eight times, every time somebody drags a slider in the skin editor.
What this does NOT do is tell a client how to draw. There is no window frame here, no button shape, no font. A client that wants to look like it belongs uses these colours in its own drawing; a client that wants to look like itself ignores them. Neither is wrong, and a protocol that tried to enforce the first would be a toolkit pretending to be a protocol.

interface.name: recon_theme_manager_v1
interface.description: A global. Binding it gets one theme object, which begins by sending everything and then sends again on every change.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Existing theme objects are unaffected; this is only the factory.

request.name: get_theme

description.summary: ask to be told the palette

request.description: The new object sends `palette`, `metrics` and `done` immediately, so a client can draw its first frame without waiting for anything to change.

interface.name: recon_theme_v1

description.summary: the palette, and changes to it

interface.description: Every change arrives as palette, then metrics, then done. A client should redraw on `done` rather than on each of the others -- the two arrive together and redrawing twice for one change is a visible flicker on a slow client.

event.name: palette
event.description:
An array of 32-bit ARGB values, in ReconOS's role order. A client that does not know the order can still use the first few, which are the window frame and its title -- but the honest way to read this is against the header that names them.
The count is whatever this version of the protocol carries. A client should check it rather than assuming, because a compositor may be older than the client is.

arg.name: colours
arg.summary: ARGB, one per role, in order

event.name: metrics

description.summary: the numbers that are not colours

event.description:
Title bar height, border thickness, corner radius and the rest, in the same fixed order and with the same versioning rule as the palette.
Sent as a second array rather than folded into the first because they are not colours and a client reading past the end of one into the other would get a number that looks plausible.

arg.name: values
arg.summary: int32, one per metric, in order

event.name: name
event.description: For a client that wants to say so, or to keep something cached per skin. Not for deciding how to draw: a skin named "Midnight" may be edited to be pale, and a client that switched on the name rather than on the colours would then be wrong in a way nothing corrects.

event.name: done

description.summary: that is the whole of this change

event.description: Everything sent since the last `done` belongs together. Redraw here.
